headline: The audit found one fact that reframes both this reconstruction and the retirement that preceded it: Institution Spaces and the 'legacy correspondence family' ARE THE SAME CODE. `/institution/:institutionId/spaces/:spaceId` and `/me/correspondence/:spaceId` both build `SpaceScreen`, distinguished only by whether an institutionId is passed. Retiring the correspondence family as previously scoped would have deleted the Institution Spaces product outright.

founderRulingRecorded.ruling: Legacy personal correspondence history and legacy Institution Space message history have no strategic value sufficient to block reconstruction or retirement. They must not block reconstruction, force compatibility architecture, force history-copy migrations, force dual-runtime support, consume substantial implementation time, or dictate the new product model.
founderRulingRecorded.supersedes: The migration-first assumption in the CO-RC-C7-005 readiness audit. That record is preserved as written; this is the superseding interpretation forward.
founderRulingRecorded.effect: `node scripts/migrate-conversations.js` is HELD and was NOT run. The 78 legacy message rows (9 direct + 67 personal-space + 2 institution-space) do not justify architecture.
founderRulingRecorded.unchanged: No production data was deleted, and none is authorized. Legacy rows may remain inert and become unreachable.

decisiveFinding.statement: Institution Spaces run on the legacy correspondence runtime. They are not a separate system.
evidence: lib/router.dart:1564 — `/me/correspondence/:spaceId` builds the SAME `SpaceScreen` without institutionId.

space_screen.dart:85-92 — the class documents this itself: institutionId is 'Present only when this Space is owned by an institution … Governs which backend authority/endpoint this screen reads through.'
lib/router.dart:1860 — the institution thread route builds `ThreadStateWrapper`, the same correspondence thread surface as `/me/correspondence/:spaceId/thread/:threadId`.

Backend: one `Space` model with a nullable `institutionId`; one `SpacesService`; personal and institution spaces differ by that column and by which controller fronts them (`spaces.controller.ts` vs `institution-spaces.controller.ts`).
decisiveFinding.consequenceForRetirement: The prior readiness audit classified `space_screen.dart` (1 identity site) and the correspondence thread surfaces as retirement-owned under CO-RC-C7-005. That classification was correct about the FILE and wrong about the CONSEQUENCE: those files also constitute the live Institution Spaces product. They are RECONSTRUCTION-OWNED, not merely retirement-owned. Phase 5 cannot delete them until Institution Spaces has a replacement surface.
decisiveFinding.reclassification: space_screen.dart moves from RETIREMENT-OWNED to RECONSTRUCTION-OWNED. The 15-site count is unchanged — the site still exists and is still discharged by eventual deletion — but what discharges it is now this reconstruction, not the correspondence retirement.

institutionSpaceMembership.content: Two capabilities that are never synonyms and never share an implementation. ADD MEMBER: an authorized Space admin directly grants membership to an eligible EXISTING member of the owning institution — no invitation, no consent step. INVITE PERSON: the governed invitation lifecycle, for people not directly eligible or external to the institution.
institutionSpaceMembership.frozenBoundary: Space membership must NEVER become a backdoor into Institution membership. Adding someone to a Space never grants, implies or infers Institution membership.
institutionSpaceMembership.implication: The reconstructed Space MUST retain an admin-governed membership model with roles and direct add. This is not optional and not re-openable.

conversationCanon.originNotGovernance: 'ORIGIN ≠ GOVERNANCE. startedByUserId is historical provenance only. No creator-owner, creator-host, or creator-admin semantics exist.'
conversationCanon.removalAbsent: 'v1 participant management: anyone may leave, always; participant removal is intentionally ABSENT in v1 … if production use proves group safety requires removal, it arrives as an explicitly modeled TRANSFERABLE STEWARDSHIP primitive — never invitation provenance masquerading as governance, NEVER ROLE VOCABULARY ON ORDINARY CONVERSATIONS.'
conversationCanon.institutionConstraints: 'institution↔institution EXPLICITLY REFUSED'; person→institution initiation only where the follow/consent relationship permits.
conversationCanon.c7Charter: 'C7 (amended): INSTITUTIONAL CONVERSATION & DESK on this system.' So building institutional communication on Conversation is already the chartered direction.
conversationCanon.dualAttribution: Every institutional message preserves HUMAN ACTOR alongside the institution voice — `ConversationMessage.speakingForInstitutionId` with `senderUserId`.

frozenDoctrineThatConstrainsThis.THE_TENSION: An Institution Space is a GOVERNED GROUP: admin-added members, six roles, visibility settings, institutional ownership. The Conversation canon deliberately REFUSES role vocabulary, creator-admin semantics and participant removal on conversations. These two frozen doctrines cannot both describe the same object. This is the central architectural decision of the reconstruction, and it is a founder decision, not an engineering one.

D1_governance.ruling: OPTION A. Space governs membership and access; Conversation provides the communication runtime for the admitted population. Conversation parties on a space-backed conversation are derived from Space membership and are never an independent competing membership authority.
D1_governance.implemented: src/spaces/institution-space-conversation.authority.ts — ONE synchronisation boundary, as the ruling required, rather than SpaceMember->ConversationParty writes scattered through handlers.
D1_governance.canonUntouched: No role vocabulary was added to conversations, no creator-admin semantics, and no removal governance entered the Conversation domain. Setting leftAt when a Space removes a member is the projection reporting that the person no longer belongs to the Space; an ordinary conversation has no Space to project from, so the canon's 'removal is intentionally ABSENT in v1' still holds exactly as written.
D1_governance.reconciliationNotDelta: syncParties reconciles the WHOLE party set against current membership. A delta is correct only if every mutation path remembers to call it; a reconciliation is correct even after one forgot. Pinned by a test that applies three membership changes with zero notifications and still converges.

D2_cardinality.ruling: ONE Institution Space -> ONE canonical Conversation. No channels. Thread is not preserved as a disguised channel abstraction.
D2_cardinality.implemented: Space.conversationId (nullable, unique, FK) + migration 20260905000000_institution_space_conversation. createInstitutionSpace no longer creates a Thread — the `threads: { create: ... }` block is deleted, not renamed.
D2_cardinality.lazyCreation: The conversation is created on first need rather than eagerly, so Spaces that predate this architecture work without a production backfill, which is not authorised.

D3_realtime.ruling: Realtime implementation deferred; realtime ARCHITECTURE not deferred.

The reconstructed surface reuses ConversationScreen, which already carries the canonical realtime entry points, so when group realtime is activated it arrives through RealtimeSessionSurfaceType.CONVERSATION for Spaces exactly as for any other conversation. Nothing in this slice would have to be undone.

backend.newAuthority: src/spaces/institution-space-conversation.authority.ts — ensureConversation / syncParties / onMemberAdded / onMemberRemoved / onSpaceLifecycleChanged. Every operation idempotent. Race on conversation creation resolved by a conditional updateMany claim; the loser adopts the winner's conversation and deletes its own rather than orphaning one.
backend.schema: Space.conversationId String? @unique with FK to Conversation (onDelete: SetNull), plus the reciprocal relation on Conversation. Migration is purely additive: one nullable column, one unique index, one guarded FK. No row is written, no legacy table altered, no message migrated.

backend.newCapability: removeInstitutionSpaceMember — the mirror of the frozen Add Member doctrine, which the legacy product never had. mapping.registerText: The 'Ready to join' affordance persisted after the call had ended. A 12s re-hydrate plus a controller terminal-clear were deployed; proof is outstanding.
mapping.whatTheScreenshotsAdd: The outstanding live proof — and it is NEGATIVE. Screenshot 1 (2026-08-17, /messages, 'Video call') and screenshot 3 (2026-08-20, /institution/:id/spaces, 'Audio call') both sit at 'Ready to join / Tap Join call to enter' with Join call and Leave offered. The deployed remedy has not resolved it on either surface.
mapping.institutionSpacesChangesScope: NO. It adds a second consumer through which the same defect is observable.
mapping.recommendation: F044 stays IMPLEMENTED_NOT_LIVE_CERTIFIED and should NOT advance; this is live evidence AGAINST the deployed fix, so its proof obligation is now failed rather than merely outstanding.

mapping.registerText: Roster count versus actually-connected count. The presentation half shipped but media-connected domain truth is untouched. Section K verdict: 'Not harmless for call truth.'
mapping.whatTheScreenshotsAdd: Direct visual confirmation on both surfaces: the header badge reads 2 participants while the viewer has not joined and no media is connected. Exactly the roster-vs-connected divergence the finding describes.

mapping.registerText: The incoming-ring card rendered with an ugly yellow underline. Root cause: a missing Material ancestor in the root overlay (dfc9027).
mapping.whatTheScreenshotsAdd: Screenshot 2 (/messages/c/:id) shows the incoming-call overlay — the founder's 'redbox pill' — with the yellow underline on all three lines ('Incoming video call', the caller name, 'started a video call'), alongside the red decline and accept controls. Founder attests this overlay is UNCHANGED in the live product, so it is current evidence.
mapping.institutionSpacesChangesScope: NO — the ring card is the personal conversation surface. Ownership unchanged.
mapping.recommendation: F047 stays IMPLEMENTED_NOT_LIVE_CERTIFIED and must NOT advance. Its outstanding proof is now FAILED rather than merely outstanding: the deployed Material-ancestor fix has not resolved the presentation. Same disposition as F044 — deployed remedy, negative live evidence.
mapping.correctionOfMyEarlierReading: I first recorded this as ambiguous because the fix commit dfc9027 shares the screenshot's date, and I reasoned the capture might predate deployment. The founder has since confirmed the behaviour is unchanged live. The caveat is withdrawn: this is not an undated artefact, it is the current state.

mapping.finding: F045 — Accept freezes/spins on later calls
mapping.registerText: Root cause RC-B: the overlay mounted above the router never unmounts, so `_joining` stays latched true after navigation.
mapping.whyMentioned: The founder's term for the incoming-call card is the 'redbox pill (overlay)', and F045's recorded root cause RC-B is precisely that overlay: 'the overlay mounted above the router never unmounts'. Both persisted call surfaces also appear over LIST routes (/messages and /institution/:id/spaces), which is the same mechanism. Offered as a plausible shared mechanism with F044 and F047 — NOT a confirmed reproduction, since the founder reported no accept freeze and I have no evidence of one.
mapping.recommendation: No state change. Flagged prominently for whoever repairs F044/F047: one overlay that never unmounts may explain the persisted ready-to-join surface, the unchanged ring presentation and RC-B together. Worth testing as one mechanism before treating them as three repairs.

genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.status: ONE BEHAVIOUR IS GENUINELY ABSENT. Reported rather than forced into an approximate finding, and NO id was invented.
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.founderReport: "after accept it should move to call not this mediator" — and "this overlay becomes more ugly in the mobile experience, its reception side, after accept".
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.defect: On the RECEPTION side, accepting an incoming call does not put the callee into the call. It delivers them to the pre-join surface — 'Ready to join / Tap Join call to enter' — where they must press Join a second time. Accept and Join are presented as two separate acts when accepting IS the intent to join.
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.structuralConfirmation: There is NO auto-join path anywhere in lib/features/realtime. 'Ready to join' at realtime_room_screen.dart:1413 is a terminal pre-join stage whose only exit is a manual tap, and a grep for autoJoin/shouldAutoJoin returns nothing. So this is not an intermittent failure — the callee lands on the mediator by construction, every time.

whyThisIsNotAnExistingFinding.notF044: F044 is 'Ready-to-join persists AFTER THE CALL HAD ENDED' — a lingering affordance with a different trigger. This is the surface appearing after ACCEPT, when a call is starting.
whyThisIsNotAnExistingFinding.notF045: F045 is Accept FREEZING or SPINNING — a dead button. Here Accept works; it simply delivers the user to the wrong place.
whyThisIsNotAnExistingFinding.notF071: F071 is accept/reject defective on RELEASED NATIVE BINARIES, BLOCKED pending a store release. This is present in the web client.
whyThisIsNotAnExistingFinding.notF041: F041 is a false 'Connection lost' pre-join state, LIVE_CERTIFIED. Different state, different message.

genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.doctrineCheck: The frozen ACCEPT/DECLINE truth-propagation doctrine requires that RINGING -> ACCEPTED -> JOINING -> CONNECTED are never COLLAPSED as model states. It does NOT require the human to press two buttons. A repair that carries the callee automatically from ACCEPTED through JOINING to CONNECTED keeps every state distinct and violates nothing. Recorded so a future repair is not talked out of it by a doctrine that does not actually forbid it.
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.mobileAggravation: The founder reports the overlay is materially worse on mobile on the reception side after accept. Whether that is a distinct responsive defect or the same mediator rendered badly at narrow width is not established, and is not asserted here.
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.minorObservationNotInflated: The pre-join surface uses Icons.call_rounded regardless of kind, which is why a 'Video call' header appears beside a phone icon. Noted; too small to be its own finding.
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.accountingImplication: Issuing this as a new finding would move the register from 143 findings / 451 units to 144 / 452. That is a founder decision about a FOUNDER_RATIFIED baseline, not an engineering one, so no id was assigned and no total was changed. The register still validates at 143 + 308 = 451 across 17 chapters.
genuinelyAbsentFromRegister.requestedDecision: Issue an id for this defect (or direct that it be absorbed into an existing finding whose scope you intend to widen).

inheritedCallingDefects.notF036: F036 (Stuck in 'Connecting' forever, LIVE_CERTIFIED) is a DIFFERENT state and was not observed. 'Ready to join' is a pre-join affordance, not a connecting state, and conflating them would have wrongly reopened a certified finding.
inheritedCallingDefects.repairBoundary: Any eventual repair belongs to the canonical Conversation/Thread calling authority, so ONE repair corrects personal, public and Institution Space behaviour together. No SpaceCall, Space-specific call lifecycle, Space-specific controls, duplicate realtime state or Space-local participant/session semantics is to be created.
inheritedCallingDefects.meetingsBoundary: UNTOUCHED and not implicated. None of these findings concerns Meetings, and Conversation and Meetings realtime semantics are not to be merged because they present similar concepts. 52 Meetings tests pass.
inheritedCallingDefects.evidenceCurrency: FOUNDER CLARIFICATION 2026-08-20: all three screenshots are CURRENT. The founder did not re-capture the incoming-call overlay — the 'REDBOX PILL (OVERLAY)' in their words — because it is unchanged in the live product: 'redbox pill (overlay) in old screenshot is same in new... the experience is still same'. The 2026-08-17 timestamps record when the images were taken, not the age of the behaviour they show. Founder first-hand attestation from the person running the product is the same class of evidence live certification already relies on.
inheritedCallingDefects.summaryAfterClarification: Three existing findings now carry NEGATIVE live evidence against deployed remedies — F044 (ready-to-join persists), F047 (ring-card presentation), and F035 (roster vs connected count, which never claimed a fix). None is an Institution Spaces defect, none is new, and no duplicate ID was created. What changed with the founder's clarification is the strength of the evidence, not its ownership.
